content.title: About
content.content: Ravioli are small pasta parcels filled with a seasoned blend of beef, pork, or a mixture of both. They are served hot in a fragrant tomato sauce or meat sauce, making the dish hearty and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ravioli originated in Italy and have been prepared for over 800 years.
There are more than 30 regional filling variations, ranging from classic meat to cheese and vegetable blends.
The tomatoes used in the sauce are often the sweet San Marzano variety.
Ravioli are traditionally served as a "primo" (first course) in an Italian meal.
In some regions, ravioli are shaped like a flower, with two half‑circles joined at the center.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat filling provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and pork contain heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B12, B6, and niacin support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Moderate healthy fats
items.content: Lean meat provides monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Fatty cuts of meat can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The pasta dough contains wheat gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Ravioli are energy‑dense; portions should be moderated for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve ravioli hot, drizzled with tomato or meat sauce. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or oregano. They pair well with a light arugula salad dressed with olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry ravioli in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months. Cooked ravioli last 2–3 days in the refrigerator and up to 2 months in the freezer.
